# Acacia Pappas

Software engineer. Former educator. Currently serving as interim CTO at Hope Street Group. I like building and creating. Tools of choice: words, languages, computers, story, pencil and paper, and more recently any number of large language models.

## About

This site is a personal engineering portfolio. It tracks questions I'm wrestling with, things I've figured out, and work that came out of it.

## Now

- Scaling Hope AI through capability, distribution, and context (August 2026) — The story of building Hope AI from a career-advisor chatbot into a classroom platform serving 20,000+ students across 300+ schools, told through three evolving bottlenecks: model capability, institutional distribution, and local context. Built against the ChatGPT adoption boom from November 2022 through June 2026.

## Writing

- From Educator to Engineer: How the I/Own It Scholarship Launched my Career in Tech (2018) — career transition from teaching to software engineering via Hack Reactor and Optimizely.
- Building Reliable Applications in the New Age of Non-Deterministic Data (2024) — Fluttercon EU talk on building resilient Flutter apps that consume LLM-generated data, covering prompting, temperature/top-p tuning, function calling, validation, defaults/sanitation, and moderation.
- AI Philosophy (2024) — Hope Street Group's internal statement on AI, the future, and how the org does and does not build education technology powered by LLMs, covering safety, bias mitigation, teacher adoption burden, student privacy, and AI literacy.
